method: A 400 m oval is two equal straights joined by two semicircles, so the lane 1 measurement radius is (400 - 2 x straight) / 2pi. Lanes 2 and outward are measured 20 cm from the line on their inside edge, while lane 1 is measured 30 cm from the kerb or, where there is no kerb, 20 cm from a painted line. The 400 m stagger for lane n is therefore 2pi x ((n - 1) x lane width + 0.20 - lane 1 offset): with 1.22 m lanes off a 30 cm kerb that gives 7.04, 14.70, 22.37, 30.03, 37.70, 45.36 and 53.03 m, and measuring lane 1 from a painted line instead gives 7.67, 15.33, 23.00, 30.66, 38.33, 45.99 and 53.66 m. Each lane's 400 m length is 400 m plus its stagger, and the 200 m stagger is half the 400 m figure because a 200 m race covers one bend. The inner edge radius is the lane 1 measurement radius minus its offset, the outer radius adds one lane width per lane, and the running-surface area is the ring between those radii plus the two straights. Inputs are 2 to 10 lanes, a lane width of 0.9 to 1.5 m and straights of 40 to 120 m. This is planning arithmetic only: it assumes a two-straight 400 m oval, and it does not survey a track, set competition markings or certify a facility. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: 400 m standard track: two equal straights and two semicircular bends, with the lane 1 measurement line 30 cm from the kerb, or 20 cm from a painted line when there is no kerb
Lanes 2 and outward are measured 20 cm from the inside line, so a 1.22 m lane adds 2pi x 1.12 m of stagger after lane 2 instead of a full lane width of arc
Published 400 m start staggers for a 1.22 m lane width are 7.04, 14.70, 22.37, 30.03, 37.70, 45.36 and 53.03 m
